titel: Commodities, real estate and tangible assets
kurz: Why there is always a legal wrapper between the investor and the physical asset, and why this wrapper often matters more than the asset itself.

bloecke.md:
Commodities, real estate and collectibles cannot be booked into a securities account like a share. This shared characteristic determines how you can invest in them. A barrel of crude oil has to be stored and insured, and at some point someone has to take delivery of it. A flat cannot be divided into a thousand parts, and a painting exists only once.

There is therefore always a legal wrapper between the investor and the physical asset: a futures contract, a debt security, segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen) or a public limited company. This wrapper often influences return, tax, insolvency protection and tradability more strongly than the price of the asset itself. An analysis that only looks at the oil price or the rental market therefore covers only half of the picture.

## Commodities as futures contracts

A commodity fund does not own any commodities in physical form. It holds futures contracts, that is agreements to take a certain quantity at a fixed price on a fixed date. Because nobody wants delivery, the fund has to sell each expiring contract before maturity and buy one that matures later. This switch is called rolling. Depending on the shape of the futures curve, rolling costs money or brings money in. This has nothing to do with the direction of the commodity price.

bloecke.formel: Futures price ≈ Spot price + Storage costs + Interest costs − Availability premium
bloecke.erklaerung: If storage costs and forgone interest predominate, the futures price is above the spot price (contango). If the commodity is scarce and immediate access to it is worth a lot, the futures price is below the spot price (backwardation).
variablen: Rent, insurance, wastage up to the delivery date
Interest forgone on the money tied up in the inventory
Value that a processor places on immediate access to the commodity (convenience yield)

bloecke.titel: Two futures curves with the same spot price
bloecke.unter: Schematic illustration with a premium or discount of 0.4% per month; in contango, the fund buys at a higher price with every roll, in backwardation at a lower price.

bloecke.md: [[Contango]] means that the later contract is more expensive than the current one. The fund then sells cheaply and buys expensively with every roll. [[Backwardation]] is the opposite case, in which the fund gains a little with each switch. Which state prevails depends on storage costs, the level of interest rates and scarcity. Industrial metals with expensive storage tend towards contango, while energy and agricultural markets switch between the two states depending on inventory levels.

bloecke.titel: Roll costs at a constant price
bloecke.md:
The current contract is quoted at 80.00, the next one at 80.32. That corresponds to a premium of 0.40%. The fund rolls monthly, and both the curve and the spot price remain unchanged.

Roll result over twelve months: 1 ÷ (1.004^12) − 1 = −4.68%.

With a premium of 0.8% per month, it is −9.1%; with 0.2%, only −2.4%. This is offset by income that is easily overlooked. A futures contract only ties up margin, and the rest of the fund assets are invested at interest. With the ECB deposit facility rate at 2.50% (since 16 September 2026), this interest income once again makes a noticeable contribution to the result; during the zero interest rate period, this was not the case.

bloecke.titel: Return components of a commodity index
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation in percentage points; although the commodity becomes more expensive, the investor earns nothing.

bloecke.md: Marketing material and the news show the spot price, but investors cannot buy at that price. What counts for the portfolio is the index performance including all roll results and after deducting fund costs. In long periods of contango, the two curves diverge by double-digit percentages. Before buying a commodity product, you should therefore clarify which index is tracked and how it rolls. Some indices deliberately roll into contracts further out in order to dampen the effect.

## Gold as an exception

Gold does not perish, and a safe-deposit box costs little in relation to its value. This makes physical backing possible here, which is ruled out for wheat or natural gas. However, European fund law stands in the way of a gold fund. The UCITS (OGAW) rules, implemented in Germany in the KAGB (German Investment Code), require diversification and prohibit direct investment in commodities. A fund that holds only gold is not permitted as a UCITS ETF.

The industry therefore uses the [[Exchange-traded commodity (ETC)|ETC]]. This is a bearer bond (Inhaberschuldverschreibung) that is collateralised with gold bars and often securitises a claim to delivery. An ETC does not constitute segregated fund assets. The investor has a claim against an issuer that is economically secured by the deposited metal but is legally structured differently from a fund. On 31 July 2026, a physically backed gold ETC with a volume of €29.5 billion was among the ten largest exchange-traded products in Europe. It was the only product on this list that is not a fund. In September 2026, Deutsche Börse listed 205 ETCs and 361 ETNs in addition to 2,971 ETFs.

Physical gold is covered by the rules on private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) in Section 23(1) no. 2 EStG (Income Tax Act). After a holding period of twelve months, the gain is tax-free; within this period, an exemption threshold (Freigrenze) of €1,000 applies to all private disposal transactions in the year. In a 2015 ruling on Xetra-Gold, the Federal Fiscal Court (BFH) decided that an ETC with a claim to delivery is treated like the metal for tax purposes. Without a delivery claim, it is classed as a miscellaneous capital receivable (sonstige Kapitalforderung) under Section 20(2) EStG, on which 26.375% flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) plus church tax is due. In practice, some custodian banks withhold tax even on ETCs with a delivery claim; the correction is then made via the capital income schedule of the tax return (Anlage KAP).

bloecke.md:
## Real estate in the portfolio

There are three fundamentally different ways to add real estate to a portfolio.

An **open-ended real estate fund** is a pool of segregated fund assets whose holdings are valued by appraisers and not on a stock exchange. Since the KAGB, fixed periods have applied: a minimum holding period of 24 months and a notice period of twelve months before units are returned to the company (Section 255 KAGB). Units can be sold on the stock exchange at any time, but at the price a buyer is willing to pay. In times of stress, this price is below the unit value. For tax purposes, a partial exemption of 60% applies, or 80% for predominantly foreign properties (Section 20(3) InvStG).

**[[Real estate investment trust (REIT)|REITs]]** are public limited companies that are exempt from corporation tax and trade tax (Gewerbesteuer) at company level. In return, they must distribute at least 90% of their profits and hold predominantly real estate. Because there is no prior tax burden at company level, no partial exemption applies for the investor; the dividend is fully subject to flat-rate withholding tax.

The third route is **real estate shares** and ETFs on them, that is ordinary shares. Vonovia or a global real estate index reacts to interest rates, leverage and sentiment like any other company. The share price is linked to the value of the properties, but only loosely, and financial leverage amplifies this link.

An open-ended real estate fund reports an almost straight-line performance over many years. This is due to the valuation method and not to lower risk. Appraisals are carried out at regular intervals and change slowly, whereas a stock exchange price changes by the second. The fluctuations do not disappear as a result; they are merely booked later. Anyone who takes the smoothed series as a sign of low risk is confusing the measurement method with the performance of the properties. In a crisis, a second problem arises. Units that can be redeemed daily in a portfolio of properties that takes months to sell are a contradiction in the construction. The periods in the KAGB arose from this contradiction.

## Forests, art, wine, classic cars

These assets cannot be valued according to the rules of the capital market, because they have no ongoing income that could be estimated in advance (with the exception of forests, whose income arises in long cycles). Instead, they incur ongoing costs: storage at the right temperature, insurance, restoration, appraisals, garage fees.

The common return indices for art or wine are almost all based on auction results. Objects that are not consigned or do not find a buyer do not appear in them. Repeated sales of the same object are rare, and items that promise a gain are preferentially consigned. The published return is therefore systematically biased upwards and is also calculated before costs. In addition, there is the risk regarding authenticity and provenance, a market without binding price determination and expertise that has to be acquired over years or bought in at a high price.

For tax purposes, collectibles count as other assets (andere Wirtschaftsgüter) under Section 23 EStG and are tax-free after one year. For art, the artist's resale right (Folgerecht) also applies when a work is resold through a dealer or auctioneer (Section 26 UrhG, Copyright Act). Anyone planning to build wealth with collectibles should know these costs before assessing the return.

bloecke.md:
## Tangible assets and inflation protection

In sales, “tangible asset” is used as a synonym for inflation protection, which is not accurate. Protection against currency depreciation only arises where cash flows grow along with prices, for example with rent under an index clause, a company with pricing power or a forest whose timber becomes more expensive. Where there is no cash flow, the return consists solely of the price the next buyer pays, and this price depends on the real interest rate.

For 2026, this can be quantified well. On 17 September 2026, ten-year US inflation-linked bonds yielded 2.61% in real terms, and ten-year German federal bonds (Bunds) yielded 3.55% in nominal terms, with consumer price inflation in Germany at 2.9% in August. Investors who hold gold or a painting forgo this real return. During the zero interest rate period, forgoing it cost nothing. In mid-September 2026 it cost dollar investors just over two and a half percentage points a year, and euro investors around 0.6 percentage points after deducting the August inflation rate. This does not speak against tangible assets, but it sets the minimum return a tangible asset must achieve to pay off.

bloecke.titel: Four checks when buying tangible assets
bloecke.md:
1. Clarify what you hold in legal terms (segregated fund assets, debt security, share or a physical object).
2. Clarify whether the return comes from a cash flow or only from the price at the next sale.
3. Calculate the costs of a complete cycle of purchase, holding period and sale as a percentage of the amount invested.
4. Estimate how long the exit takes in the worst case and what discount it involves.

mitnehmen: There is always a legal wrapper between the investor and the asset, and it often determines insolvency protection, tax and availability more strongly than the price of the asset.
Commodities are held in the portfolio as futures contracts, and the roll result can completely offset the price development regardless of the direction of the spot price.
Gold ETCs are debt securities and not funds; whether a claim to delivery is securitised determines whether they are taxed under Section 23 instead of Section 20 EStG.
The smooth line of an open-ended real estate fund comes from valuation by appraisers and not from lower risk; in return, investors must observe the statutory periods under Section 255 KAGB.
A tangible asset does not equal inflation protection, because without a cash flow that grows along with prices, the only counterpart to owning it is forgoing today's real interest rate.

begriffe.text: State of a futures curve in which contracts maturing later are more expensive than the current one. Rolling then means selling cheaply and buying expensively, so that value is lost continuously.
State of a futures curve in which the contract maturing later is cheaper than the current one, usually when the commodity is scarce. Rolling then makes a positive contribution.
Contribution to the result that arises solely from switching from an expiring futures contract into one that matures later, regardless of how the spot price develops.
Exchange Traded Commodity, an exchange-traded bearer bond on a commodity, usually physically backed. Since an ETC does not constitute segregated fund assets, it depends on the issuer.
Real estate company in the form of a public limited company that is tax-exempt at company level and in return must distribute most of its profit and hold predominantly real estate.
Asset with physical substance. The term says nothing about inflation protection; what matters for that is whether there is a cash flow that grows with the price level.
